conversation.text: It would have made no difference if it happened a month ago, right? I’m not just jealous of you two. I feel like everyone has the ability to feel a bit of envy. They are like my enemies.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Mara, I remember the wedding we were supposed to attend last year. I was just surprised by how many people showed up. You two look like you can get together, and that’s not fair at all.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Mara, don't give me that shit. You go cold for five minutes and act like I'm supposed to pretend I don't notice.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Jules, you're wrong and smug about it, which is almost impressive. Explain the disputed tattoo pact without embarrassing yourself.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: You're worse at hiding motives than Mara, Mara. the disputed tattoo pact proved that already.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I don't need you to prove the pact, Owen, because I'm being real about how you feel about the situation right now. Let's do this the easy way.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: The fake wedding in Duluth made me a little uncomfortable, and I'm just saying to be safe here and trust my intuition that Owen, I can take on this.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: I really value my ability to look in the back of the crowd and trust people, no matter their backgrounds. And you, aren't you, have you tried it before with different subjects?

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: I would have to talk to a liar at this rate in order to impress that lady and impress everyone else; I know her, trust me, the secret room behind the laundromat.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: In my next turn, I want to be the liar at this rate to get ahead in a group with you, you're a big, trust me, trust me, secret room behind the laundromat.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: No, Jules. That's bullshit, and the birthday-cake sabotage is exactly why I don't trust your version of anything.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: No, Jules. I'm sure I don't trust your version of anything, but it’s really cool. You're one of the best in my league. I know my friends at the club will love me right here, there, everywhere!

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: We need to keep our pact secret if I truly am going to tell someone new that my secret is here, for now.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Now we can think more specifically. Jules, one of us cannot understand why Sarah's reaction was so different compared to our last interaction. Is this really true?

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: I feel that this is actually my reaction to the terrible karaoke blood-feud. I am a person who does not easily share secrets or keep secrets to keep the room happy. I want you to understand, in your eyes.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I apologize if I made a mistake with this conversation. I do not want you to judge me. Please let me know if there is something that I am not understanding. In your own words, please, and maybe even a link to where you can see that.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Sarah, that's bullshit. You couldn't bluff your way through the night someone stole the church bell if Herman handed you cue cards.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: In your excitement over a silly tattoo, could your rival have shown up on a dark, gloomy night? It's been called a terrible night bell! Try not to laugh this time, you would be laughed at.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Mara, that's bullshit. You don't get to dismiss me and then act surprised when I get angry about the secret room behind the laundromat.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Enough, Owen. This is beneath me. If we're going to talk, explain the fake wedding in Duluth instead of boring me.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Your rival, can we assume they’re hiding in the dark with your tattoo?

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Ah, jules, it appears your rival might have been lurking near the radio-tower beacon over the years? How did you not find it yourself?

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Owen, Jules handled the imaginary inheritance fight better than you did, and watching you pretend otherwise is embarrassing.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: The fake engagement rumor has finally found the upper hand on me and Jules! Trust is still shaky here. No more being a partner to our shared memory.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Owen, that's boring bullshit. If you want me to believe you, explain the suspicious key in Mara's coat without hiding behind that polite little act.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: That's boring bullshit. If you want me to believe you, explain the suspicious key in Mara's coat without hiding behind that polite little act. We are a team and we have a good reason to be skeptical.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Jules, this is exactly like the fake wedding in Duluth: you act confused when it's convenient and expect everyone else to swallow it.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: The suspicious key in mara's coat

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I, july, am no longer in my comfort zone. I had a dream of being caught up with you, but you left the house the next morning. I miss you deeply, but I'm not the same anymore.
